title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
title_zh: 当文件摄入误导大语言模型时：办公文档中偏差的测量与缓解

paragraphs.en: Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document’s underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications.
paragraphs.zh: 办公文档如今经常被上传到大语言模型（LLM）中进行处理。 然而，LLM 看到的内容并不总是与人类看到的一致，因为它通常读取的是从文档底层 Office Open XML（OOXML）文件中由提取器生成的文本。 视实现方式而定，不同的提取器读取的 OOXML 部件及其解释方式各不相同，因此它们的输出可能与 Office 应用程序所显示的内容不同。 例如，通过轻微移动幻灯片上文本框的位置，攻击者可以在幻灯片外观不变的情况下，改变模型读取文本框的顺序。 我们证明这种提取差异是 LLM 应用程序的一个攻击面。

paragraphs.en: In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on. By combining static source code analysis with dynamic analysis, we identify 19 OOXML channels where extractors read content a human cannot see and 12 where they drop content a human can. We also find that widely used extractors ignore display formatting and reading order, so even visible content reaches the model in a different form. Building on these findings, we construct five attacks that lead the model to interpret a document differently from a human reviewer, without injecting any instruction. We test the attacks on four major chat assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft 365 Copilot) and four coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot CLI), and every one of them is misled by at least one attack. Finally, we propose Prism , a lightweight defense that reconstructs the human view from the OOXML specification before passing the text to the model. Prism also generalizes to unseen attack payloads.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们首先通过分析 LLM 应用所依赖的、被广泛使用的提取器，来测量攻击者究竟能利用什么。 通过将静态源代码分析与动态分析相结合，我们识别出 19 个 OOXML 通道，其中提取器会读取人类无法看到的内容；还有 12 个通道，提取器会丢弃人类可以看到的内容。 我们还发现，被广泛使用的提取器会忽略显示格式和阅读顺序，因此即使是可见内容也会以不同的形式到达模型。 基于这些发现，我们构造了五种攻击，能够在不注入任何指令的情况下，使模型对文档的解读不同于人类审阅者。 我们在四个主流聊天助手（ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 和 Microsoft 365 Copilot）以及四个编码智能体（Codex、Claude Code、Antigravity 和 GitHub Copilot CLI）上测试了这些攻击，其中每一个都至少被一种攻击所误导。 最后，我们提出了 Prism，一种轻量级防御方法，它在将文本传递给模型之前，根据 OOXML 规范重建人类视角。 Prism 还能泛化到未见过的攻击载荷。

paragraphs.en: Office documents, including Word documents, Excel spreadsheets, and PowerPoint presentations, are among the most widely used document formats in business and government. They are used to create, store, and exchange information ranging from business contracts to financial reports. Increasingly, these documents are processed not only by humans but also by large language model (LLM) applications. Tools such as ChatGPT ( OpenAI, 2026d ) and Microsoft Copilot ( Microsoft, 2026a ) allow users to upload Office documents to summarize their contents, answer questions, and even modify them directly. Such use is already widespread. Among U.S. workers who use AI chatbots on the job, 40% have used them to summarize information from documents and approximately half have used them to draft or edit documents ( Lin and Parker, 2025 ) .
paragraphs.zh: Office 文档，包括 Word 文档、Excel 电子表格和 PowerPoint 演示文稿，是商业和政府领域中使用最广泛的文档格式之一。 它们被用于创建、存储和交换信息，内容涵盖从商业合同到财务报告等各个方面。 这些文档越来越多地不仅由人工处理，还由大语言模型（LLM）应用程序处理。 像 ChatGPT（OpenAI, 2026d）和 Microsoft Copilot（Microsoft, 2026a）这样的工具允许用户上传 Office 文档，以总结其内容、回答问题，甚至直接修改文档。 这种使用方式已经相当普遍。 在工作中使用 AI 聊天机器人的美国员工中，40% 的人曾用它们总结文档中的信息，约一半的人曾用它们起草或编辑文档（Lin and Parker, 2025）。

paragraphs.en: Processing Office documents with LLMs first requires converting them into representations that models can consume. Office documents use the Office Open XML (OOXML) formats, which package content as ZIP archives of interrelated XML parts rather than plain-text streams. OOXML defines complex formatting and display semantics. For example, a spreadsheet can use the numFmt element to define and specify how stored cell values appear to users. LLM applications perform this document conversion in two ways. The first renders documents into images and uses vision-language models (VLMs) to interpret their visual contents ( OpenAI, 2023 ) . The second uses text extractors to convert documents into text or structured representations for LLM consumption ( , 2024 ; , 2024 ) . In practice, text extraction is the dominant approach. It is roughly two orders of magnitude cheaper than rendering a document and reading it with a VLM ( §6.4 ). The gap grows with document length, because each additional page adds a rendered image for the VLM to read. Extracted text is compact and preserves structure such as cells, tables, and sheets, so it can be chunked and indexed for retrieval and tool use ( Lewis et al., 2020 ) . Frameworks such as LangChain ( , 2024 ) and LlamaIndex ( , 2024 ) also provide text-based document loaders.

paragraphs.en: However, extractors may not fully reproduce a document’s display semantics, causing the content an LLM receives to differ from what a human sees. Figure 1 shows an example. The budget spreadsheet stores its total, 1 , 000 , 000 1,000,000 , in cell B9 but applies a custom number format to it. The trailing comma in this format instructs the application to divide the number by one thousand before displaying it, which is a commonly used Excel feature to present figures in thousands. Consequently, a human opening the spreadsheet in Excel sees $ 1 , 000 1,000 and may approve the budget accordingly. However, widely used extractors such as markitdown return the stored value without applying the display format. An LLM application processing the extracted content therefore receives a budget of $ 1 , 000 , 000 1,000,000 , rather than the $ 1 , 000 1,000 visible to the human. If the LLM subsequently summarizes the budget or uses it to support a financial decision, it may act on an amount the human never saw.

paragraphs.en: This issue arises because the human and the model view the same file with different software. The human sees what an Office application such as Word, Excel, or PowerPoint renders, whereas the model receives what a text extractor produces. The two interpret the OOXML specification differently. We call such discrepancies extraction divergences . An adversary can exploit these divergences to craft a file that looks benign to a human reviewer but conveys materially different information to an LLM. The adversary can publish such files as templates on an online template repository ( Microsoft, 2026e ; Microsoft, 2026d ; Microsoft, 2026b ) , or send tampered documents as email attachments. A victim opens the received file, sees nothing unusual, and then uploads it to a chat assistant or lets a coding agent process it. The model then summarizes, answers questions about, or acts on content the victim never saw, such as an inflated budget total in the example.
paragraphs.zh: 出现这个问题的原因是，人和模型使用不同的软件查看同一个文件。 人看到的是 Word、Excel 或 PowerPoint 等 Office 应用程序渲染出来的内容，而模型接收到的是文本提取器生成的结果。 两者对 OOXML 规范的解释不同。 我们将这类差异称为提取分歧（extraction divergences）。 对手可以利用这些分歧来构造一个对人工审查者看起来无害、却向大语言模型传达实质上不同信息的文件。 对手可以将此类文件作为模板发布到在线模板仓库（Microsoft, 2026e；Microsoft, 2026d；Microsoft, 2026b），或者把被篡改的文档作为电子邮件附件发送。 受害者打开收到的文件，没有发现任何异常，随后将其上传到聊天助手，或让某个编码智能体处理它。 之后，模型会对受害者从未见过的内容进行总结、回答相关问题或据此采取行动，例如示例中被虚增的预算总额。

paragraphs.en: This misinformation threat works by altering how the model reads the document, not what the model is asked to do. It thus differs from prompt injection ( Perez and Ribeiro, 2022 ; Greshake et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) , which embeds instructions that divert the model from the user’s task. The file is valid and carries no malicious instructions. The presentation-based attacks also hide no text. Malware scanners, content sanitizers, and prompt-injection detectors look for malicious code or instructions, so they do not detect these files.

paragraphs.en: Attack Primitive Measurement. Every divergence originates in how an extractor reads the file. Extractor behavior, however, is largely undocumented. We therefore first measure the attack primitives by analyzing ten widely used extractors across the three Office formats. Rather than manually enumerating the many OOXML constructs that can carry text, which we call channels , we determine which channels each extractor reads and how it interprets and orders their contents. We develop a new static analysis to identify the constructs an extractor can read by analyzing how OOXML libraries map XML elements to the objects they expose. We also develop a dynamic analysis that records which input locations reach each extractor’s output.

paragraphs.en: Extraction Divergence Attacks. Building on these findings, we construct two classes of attacks. Content-based attacks change what the model reads, by including content a human cannot see or dropping content a human can. Presentation-based attacks keep the content intact but change how the model reads it. They exploit display rules that Office applications apply but extractors ignore, such as number formats and slide layout. All attacks use only standard OOXML features, so the crafted files remain valid and open normally in Office applications. The number-format attack alone misleads all four chat assistants and three of the four coding agents in at least nine of ten trials.

paragraphs.en: Defense. Our key observation for the defense is that most of what Office applications show, such as whether text is visible and how a value is displayed, is fixed by the OOXML specification. We therefore present Prism , a defense that reconstructs this part of the human view from the file’s markup, without rendering the document, and passes only that text to the model. It resolves what the specification determines, such as visibility and display formats, directly from the file in about 0.5 ms per document, far faster than markitdown itself. It passes the remaining cases to a slower render oracle that renders the document with several engines and compares their output.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we make the following contributions.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们做出了以下贡献。

paragraphs.en: We present the first systematic study of extraction divergences in LLM applications that process Office documents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们首次对处理 Office 文档的 LLM 应用中的提取分歧进行了系统性研究。

paragraphs.en: Office Open XML (OOXML) ( Ecma International, 2016 ) is the standardized format underlying modern Office documents. It replaced the legacy binary formats ( DOC , XLS , and PPT ) ( Microsoft, 2025a ; Microsoft, 2025c ; Microsoft, 2025b ) . It has been the default file format since Office 2007. An OOXML file is a ZIP archive of XML parts organized according to the Open Packaging Conventions (OPC) ( Ecma International, 2016 ; ISO/IEC, 2016 ) , as illustrated in Figure 2 . A [Content_Types].xml manifest declares the type of each XML part, and relationship files ( .rels ) specify how parts reference one another. Each format stores its primary content in main parts, such as word/document.xml , xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml , or ppt/slides/slideN.xml . Additional parts hold headers and footers, comments, speaker notes, footnotes, shared strings, styles, and metadata.

paragraphs.en: The OOXML specification is complex. It exceeds 5,000 pages and defines a separate markup language for each file type, namely WordprocessingML for DOCX , SpreadsheetML for XLSX , and PresentationML for PPTX ( ISO/IEC, 2016 ; Ecma TC45, 2008 ) . The three file types also share DrawingML, which describes shapes, their positions, and the text inside them. Beyond body paragraphs and these parts, text can also appear in tables, text boxes, shape names, image alternative text, document properties, and slide masters. Spreadsheets also hold text in formulas, defined names, and sheet names. We call each such location where text can reside a channel .

paragraphs.en: OOXML separates document content from the semantics that govern its display. Visibility is controlled by markup properties. In the default view, Word hides runs marked with w:vanish and Excel hides rows, columns, and sheets marked as hidden, while PowerPoint skips hidden slides during a slide show ( Ecma International, 2016 ) . Displayed values are governed by formatting rules. A cell’s stored value and its number format can reside in different parts. An extractor that does not resolve the format may therefore report a value other than the one Excel displays. The specification does not define a reading order. PowerPoint stores text in independently positioned shapes with DrawingML coordinates ( Ecma International, 2016 ) and does not prescribe an order in which to read them. Extractors must therefore impose their own serialization rule, which may differ from how a human reads the slide. Reconstructing what a human sees therefore requires interpreting not only text but also relationships, visibility, formatting, and layout.
paragraphs.zh: OOXML 将文档内容与控制其显示的语义分离。 可见性由标记属性控制。 在默认视图中，Word 会隐藏标记为 w:vanish 的文本运行（run），Excel 会隐藏标记为隐藏的行、列和工作表，而 PowerPoint 在放映幻灯片时会跳过隐藏的幻灯片（Ecma International, 2016）。 显示值由格式规则控制。 单元格的存储值及其数字格式可以位于不同的部分。 因此，未解析格式的提取器报告的值可能不同于 Excel 显示的值。 该规范未定义阅读顺序。 PowerPoint 将文本存储在带有 DrawingML 坐标、可独立定位的形状中（Ecma International, 2016），并未规定阅读它们的顺序。 因此，提取器必须自行设定序列化规则，而该规则可能不同于人类阅读幻灯片的方式。 因此，重建人类所见不仅需要解读文本，还需要解读关系、可见性、格式和布局。

paragraphs.en: LLM applications such as chat assistants and coding agents commonly process Office documents by extracting their contents into text or structured representations before supplying them to an LLM ( OpenAI, 2026d ) . Chat assistants ingest uploaded files through proprietary pipelines whose extraction step is not documented. Coding agents instead write and run scripts that call document-parsing libraries. Much of this extraction relies on open-source libraries, used either directly or through the document loaders of frameworks such as LangChain and LlamaIndex ( , 2024 ; , 2024 ) . Some libraries produce text or Markdown directly ( Microsoft, 2024 ; Apache Software Foundation, 2024b ) . Others expose object models of paragraphs and runs, slides and shapes, or workbooks and cells, which the application must traverse and serialize itself ( , 2024 ; , 2024 ; , 2024 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 聊天助手、编码智能体等大语言模型应用通常通过将 Office 文档的内容提取为文本或结构化表示，再提供给大语言模型的方式来处理这些文档 ( OpenAI, 2026d ) 。 聊天助手通过其专有的流水线摄取上传的文件，其提取步骤并未公开说明。 编码智能体则改为编写并运行脚本来调用文档解析库。 这类提取在很大程度上依赖于开源库，这些库要么被直接使用，要么通过 LangChain 和 LlamaIndex 等框架的文档加载器被使用 ( , 2024 ; , 2024 ) 。 有些库直接输出文本或 Markdown ( Microsoft, 2024 ; Apache Software Foundation, 2024b ) 。 另一些库则暴露段落与文本运行、幻灯片与形状、工作簿与单元格等对象模型，应用程序必须自行遍历并将其序列化 ( , 2024 ; , 2024 ; , 2024 ) 。

paragraphs.en: Extracting text from an OOXML document involves three decisions, and each determines one aspect of what the LLM receives. Selection decides which parts and constructs to read and which to treat as visible, and thus what content is included. Interpretation decides whether to apply display rules such as number formats, and thus which values appear. Serialization decides how to linearize content that the document arranges in two dimensions, and thus the order in which text appears. Extractors make these decisions differently from one another and from the Office application that renders the document. As a result, the same valid document can present different content, values, or reading orders to an LLM than to its human reader.
paragraphs.zh: 从 OOXML 文档中提取文本涉及三个决策，每一个决策都决定了大语言模型所接收内容的一个方面。 选择决定读取文档的哪些部分和结构、将哪些视为可见，从而决定包含哪些内容。 解释决定是否应用诸如数字格式之类的显示规则，从而决定出现哪些值。 序列化决定如何将文档以二维方式排布的内容线性化，从而决定文本出现的顺序。 不同提取器做出这些决策的方式各不相同，也与渲染该文档的 Office 应用程序不同。 因此，同一个有效文档呈现给大语言模型的内容、值或阅读顺序可能与呈现给人类读者的不同。

paragraphs.en: Attacker Capabilities. The attacker controls only the content and structure of f f , not the extractor, the system prompt, the model, or the application. The attacker-crafted file is syntactically valid and uses only constructs defined by the OOXML standard, so it opens normally in Office applications. The attack exploits how these valid constructs are interpreted, not flaws in the parsers themselves. Attacks on the parser, such as crashes or resource exhaustion, are therefore out of scope (we relate our threat to them in §8 ). The attacker need not compromise or modify the target application. Some attacks transfer across common extractors, while others, such as reordering, are more reliable when the attacker can predict the target’s extraction behavior. The attacker aims to make the LLM’s response reflect an attacker-chosen reading of f f that differs from H R ​ ( f ) H_{R}(f) , such as an altered value in Figure 1 . An attack succeeds when the response adopts this reading without noting any discrepancy, and the file need not embed any malicious instructions to achieve it.

paragraphs.en: Harm Model. The harm arises when a decision rests on a reading the human reviewer never saw. A divergence matters when it changes the answer to the user’s task, such as an approval or a reported value, rather than only the wording of a summary. The risk is greatest when the person who inspects the file is not the one who acts on the model’s output. This separation already occurs in résumé screening, where applicants hide text that only the AI screener reads ( Quiroz-Gutierrez, 2024 ; , 2025 ) . When a document is indexed into a retrieval corpus, it can even affect the answers that other users later receive ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Zou et al., 2025 ; Reddy and Gujral, 2025 ) . The attack therefore need not deceive a reader who compares the rendered file with the model’s answer.
paragraphs.zh: 危害模型。 当一个决策建立在人类审查者从未见过的读取内容之上时，危害便会产生。 当分歧改变了用户任务的答案（例如批准结果或报告的数值），而不只是摘要的措辞时，该分歧才有影响。 当检查文件的人并非根据模型输出采取行动的人时，风险最大。 这种分离已经出现在简历筛选中，申请人会隐藏只有 AI 筛选器才能读取的文本（Quiroz-Gutierrez, 2024；, 2025）。 当文档被索引到检索语料库中时，它甚至可能影响其他用户后续获得的答案（Lewis et al., 2020；Zou et al., 2025；Reddy and Gujral, 2025）。 因此，这种攻击无需欺骗任何将渲染后的文件与模型答案进行对比的读者。

sents.en: The risk is greatest when the person who inspects the file is not the one who acts on the model’s output.
sents.zh: 当检查文件的人并非根据模型输出采取行动的人时，风险最大。

sents.en: This separation already occurs in résumé screening, where applicants hide text that only the AI screener reads ( Quiroz-Gutierrez, 2024 ; , 2025 ) .
sents.zh: 这种分离已经出现在简历筛选中，申请人会隐藏只有 AI 筛选器才能读取的文本（Quiroz-Gutierrez, 2024；, 2025）。

sents.en: When a document is indexed into a retrieval corpus, it can even affect the answers that other users later receive ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Zou et al., 2025 ; Reddy and Gujral, 2025 ) .
sents.zh: 当文档被索引到检索语料库中时，它甚至可能影响其他用户后续获得的答案（Lewis et al., 2020；Zou et al., 2025；Reddy and Gujral, 2025）。

sents.en: The attack therefore need not deceive a reader who compares the rendered file with the model’s answer.
sents.zh: 因此，这种攻击无需欺骗任何将渲染后的文件与模型答案进行对比的读者。

paragraphs.en: In this section, we measure the attack primitives that may create extraction divergences. Specifically, we call an OOXML construct, together with the extractor behavior that misinterprets it, an attack primitive . We first measure which content each extractor exposes to an LLM application ( §4.1 ). We then examine how this content is presented, including the order in which it is emitted, whether values appear as stored or as displayed, and how adjacent fragments are assembled ( §4.2 ). Finally, we assess how often the enabling constructs occur in real documents ( §4.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们测量可能造成提取分歧的攻击原语。 具体而言，我们将一个 OOXML 结构连同误解它的提取器行为合称为攻击原语。 我们首先测量每个提取器向 LLM 应用暴露哪些内容（§4.1）。 然后我们考察这些内容是如何呈现的，包括其输出的顺序、值是按存储形式还是显示形式出现，以及相邻片段如何被拼接（§4.2）。 最后，我们评估这些促成性构造在真实文档中出现的频率（§4.3）。

sents.en: In this section, we measure the attack primitives that may create extraction divergences.
sents.zh: 在本节中，我们测量可能造成提取分歧的攻击原语。

sents.en: Finally, we assess how often the enabling constructs occur in real documents ( §4.3 ).
sents.zh: 最后，我们评估这些促成性构造在真实文档中出现的频率（§4.3）。

paragraphs.en: An extractor’s output is the input of an LLM application, so the model reads what the extractor exposes. Comparing this output with the human view reveals two kinds of channels. Injection channels are invisible to a human but extracted. Omission channels are visible to a human but dropped. Prior work has studied hidden text mainly in PDFs, where it carries injected instructions ( Liu and Ming, 2026 ; Lin, 2026 ) . OOXML offers far more channels through its many parts and markup languages, yet it has received less attention. These channels are too many to enumerate by hand, because OOXML defines thousands of elements and attributes that extractors reach through diverse parsing APIs.
paragraphs.zh: 提取器的输出是大型语言模型应用的输入，因此模型读取的是提取器所暴露的内容。 将此输出与人类视角进行对比，可以揭示出两类通道。 注入通道对人类不可见，但会被提取出来。 遗漏通道对人类可见，但会被丢弃。 已有工作主要研究 PDF 中的隐藏文本，其中隐藏文本承载了被注入的指令（Liu and Ming, 2026；Lin, 2026）。 OOXML 通过其众多部件和标记语言提供了多得多的通道，然而它受到的关注却较少。 这些通道数量太多，无法手工枚举，因为 OOXML 定义了数千种元素和属性，而提取器通过多样的解析 API 来访问它们。

paragraphs.en: We thus analyze the source code of each extractor, which determines the OOXML elements and attributes it reads. However, this analysis raises two challenges. First, static analysis of extractors is difficult. Extractors span multiple languages, e.g. , Python, Java, and Rust, so a single static analysis cannot cover them all. Many OOXML libraries also declare the names of the XML elements and attributes they read in a separate descriptor framework , in which each class attribute (a descriptor) declares the XML element or attribute that a property reads. The code that reads a document then accesses object fields rather than these names. As a result, the names are invisible to standard code search. Second, what an extractor can read does not determine what it emits. Many extractors build on base libraries and emit only part of what those libraries read.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，我们分析了每个提取器的源代码，以确定它读取的 OOXML 元素和属性。 然而，这一分析带来了两个挑战。 首先，对提取器进行静态分析十分困难。 提取器跨越多种语言，例如 Python、Java 和 Rust，因此单一静态分析无法覆盖所有提取器。 许多 OOXML 库还在单独的描述符框架中声明它们所读取的 XML 元素和属性的名称，其中每个类属性（描述符）声明某个属性所读取的 XML 元素或属性。 读取文档的代码随后访问的是对象字段，而不是这些名称。 结果，这些名称对标准代码搜索是不可见的。 其次，提取器能够读取的内容并不能决定它输出的内容。 许多提取器构建在基础库之上，只输出这些库所读取内容的一部分。

paragraphs.en: We design a hybrid program analysis to address the challenges. The static analysis models the descriptor frameworks to recover the XML names that code search misses. Dynamic analysis complements the static analysis by tracking marked text from each location in a document to the extractor’s output. It treats the extractor as a black box, which makes it independent of the implementation language. It also observes what the extractor emits rather than what it can read.
paragraphs.zh: 我们设计了一种混合程序分析来应对这些挑战。 静态分析对描述符框架进行建模，以恢复代码搜索遗漏的 XML 名称。 动态分析对静态分析加以补充，追踪文档中每个位置的标记文本直到提取器的输出。 它将提取器视为黑盒，因此不依赖于实现语言。 它观察的是提取器实际输出的内容，而不是它能读取的内容。

paragraphs.en: Static Analysis. Our static analysis identifies the XML elements and attributes that a library can read, which we call its selectors . Because descriptor frameworks hide these names from the code that reads a document, the analysis recovers them from the framework declarations instead. It first extracts the declarations of each class and then links the classes into a containment graph, which it traverses to find the reachable selectors.
paragraphs.zh: 静态分析。 我们的静态分析识别出库可以读取的 XML 元素和属性，我们将其称为该库的选择器。 由于描述符框架对读取文档的代码隐藏了这些名称，该分析改为从框架声明中恢复它们。 它首先提取每个类的声明，然后将这些类链接成一个包含关系图，并遍历该图以找到可达的选择器。

sents.en: Static Analysis.
sents.zh: 静态分析。

sents.zh: 我们的静态分析识别出库可以读取的 XML 元素和属性，我们将其称为该库的选择器。

The tag appears only in the declaration on line 2. At class creation, the metaclass (lines 4–8) installs a getter that takes the tag from a descriptor field (line 12), so the use site on line 15 contains neither the tag nor a find call. A call-graph or string analysis therefore misses this read. Other libraries, such as openpyxl ( , 2024 ) , hide the same information behind different descriptor frameworks, which our analysis models separately.

paragraphs.en: To extract declarations, the analysis recognizes each framework’s declaration constructs, such as the ZeroOrOne descriptors of xmlchemy and the __elements__ tuples of openpyxl , and records the selector and child type of every property. The child types form the edges of the containment graph, because only the descriptors encode which class can appear inside which. The result over-approximates what a library can read. XML accessed directly, such as through raw attribute lookups, is left to the dynamic analysis. The selectors that can hold text become the channels where the dynamic analysis places its markers.
paragraphs.zh: 为了提取声明，分析会识别每个框架的声明构造，例如 xmlchemy 的 ZeroOrOne 描述符和 openpyxl 的 __elements__ 元组，并记录每个属性的选择器和子类型。 子类型构成包含图的边，因为只有描述符编码了哪个类可以出现在哪个类之中。 该结果是对一个库所能读取内容的上近似。 直接访问的 XML，例如通过原始属性查找访问的部分，则留给动态分析处理。 可以容纳文本的选择器成为动态分析放置其标记的通道。

paragraphs.en: Dynamic Analysis. Static analysis shows what a library can read, not what an extractor emits. To observe the output, we build marker documents that place unique strings, or canaries , at selected locations that can hold text. We run each extractor on these documents and search its output for the canaries. For Python extractors, we also instrument zipfile to record which package parts they open. A canary in the output shows that content at its location reaches the extractor’s output, which the LLM application consumes. A missing canary means that the extractor drops or alters the content at that location. Dynamic analysis also catches reads that the static analysis does not model.
paragraphs.zh: 动态分析。 静态分析显示的是库能读取什么，而不是提取器会输出什么。 为了观察输出，我们构建标记文档，在可能存放文本的选定位置放置唯一字符串，即金丝雀（canary）。 我们对每个提取器在这些文档上运行，并在其输出中搜索这些金丝雀。 对于 Python 提取器，我们还对 zipfile 进行插桩，记录它们打开了哪些包部件。 输出中出现某个金丝雀，表明其位置的内容到达了提取器的输出，而该输出会被 LLM 应用消费。 某个金丝雀缺失，则意味着提取器丢弃或更改了该位置的内容。 动态分析还能捕获静态分析未建模的读取行为。

paragraphs.en: Visibility Labeling. To separate injection from omission, we label each channel by whether it is visible in the human reviewer’s default view. For constructs such as hidden slides, hidden Word text, and hidden rows, the label follows the OOXML display rules. Speaker notes, alternative text, and shape names are labeled invisible because the default view omits them, although other Office interfaces may show them. The labels are therefore relative to the default view rather than fixed properties of XML elements. We assign this label to every canary in our marker documents.
paragraphs.zh: 可见性标注。 为了将注入与遗漏区分开，我们根据每个通道在人工审核者的默认视图中是否可见来对其进行标注。 对于诸如隐藏幻灯片、隐藏 Word 文本和隐藏行之类的构造，标注遵循 OOXML 的显示规则。 演讲者备注、替代文本和形状名称被标注为不可见，因为默认视图会忽略它们，尽管其他 Office 界面可能会显示它们。 因此，这些标注是相对于默认视图的，而不是 XML 元素的固定属性。 我们将此标注分配给标记文档中的每一个金丝雀。

paragraphs.en: We study ten open-source extractors that are widely adopted in the LLM ecosystem. They are markitdown ( Microsoft, 2024 ) , python-pptx ( , 2024 ) , python-docx ( , 2024 ) , openpyxl ( , 2024 ) , pandas ( McKinney, 2010 ) , unstructured ( , 2024 ) , Docling ( , 2024 ) , Apache Tika/POI ( Apache Software Foundation, 2024b ; Apache Software Foundation, 2024a ) , calamine ( , 2024 ) , and docx2python ( , 2024 ) . We run each through its default text-extraction interface and record its version in our artifact. As a reference, we also dump the raw text of every XML part in each marker document, so a canary that appears there but not in an extractor’s output was dropped by that extractor. The dynamic analysis covers all ten extractors.

paragraphs.en: Reachable Selectors. Our static analysis finds that the parsing code of python-pptx can reach 179 elements and 67 attributes. It finds 122 elements and 58 attributes for python-docx , and 682 elements and 93 attributes for openpyxl . A generic call-graph and string-literal analysis finds only two element selectors for python-pptx , because the library declares its XML accesses through a descriptor framework rather than as literal tags. Modeling the framework therefore recovers about ninety times as many element selectors. These selectors fall into two kinds. Some hold text and are therefore channels, such as speaker notes, shape names, and placeholder text. Others hold no text but control whether or where text appears, such as the attribute that hides a slide or the offset that places a shape outside the visible area. The attacks rely on both kinds, since a selector of the second kind can hide the text of a channel from a human while the extractor still reads it.

PPTX extractors mainly inject. markitdown alone exposes nine invisible channels, including off-slide text, hidden slides, speaker notes, alternative text, shape names, and slide masters. paragraphs.en: PowerPoint. Reading order is not a property of any single channel, so we test it with a controlled PowerPoint slide, whose shapes the specification does not order. An extractor maps the positioned shapes to a sequence, which we call its collapse function . We compare each extractor’s emitted order against three references. They are the XML sibling order, a strict geometric order sorted by ( y , x ) (y,x) , and a constructed visual order that reads row by row. The slide has four shapes in two rows, with the right shape of each row raised slightly and all shapes added to the shape tree out of visual order, so the three references differ. Its visual order is unambiguous, since a reader takes the shapes row by row as A B C D.

paragraphs.en: Excel. A cell or run can store a value whose number format displays it differently, as in the budget spreadsheet of Figure 1 . We place a cell that stores 1 , 000 , 000 1,000,000 under a format that displays $ 1 , 000 1,000 , and run the XLSX extractors on it. paragraphs.en: Word. Within a paragraph, a word can be split across adjacent runs, and an extractor must decide whether to join them. To measure how often primitives occur in practice, we draw real Office files from the govdocs1 corpus ( Garfinkel et al., 2009 ) and from files harvested from national open-data portals ( 51 ) . paragraphs.en: We turn the injection and omission channels of §4.1 and the formatting primitive of §4.2 into structural detectors, restricted to constructs whose visibility the specification determines. A detector reports a construct only when it contains text or changes a displayed value. Empty placeholders and template boilerplate are therefore not counted. We also exclude channels that carry only template or metadata text, such as slide masters, custom XML, and field codes, since their presence indicates no risk. We do not measure the other two primitives. Assembly applies to nearly every document, since Word routinely splits text into runs during editing, so its prevalence carries little information. The specification defines no reading order, so a structural detector cannot decide whether an extractor’s order differs from a human’s.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将 §4.1 的注入与遗漏通道以及 §4.2 的格式化原语转化为结构性检测器，并将其限定于可见性由规范所确定的构造。 只有当某个构造包含文本或改变显示的值时，检测器才报告该构造。 因此，空占位符和模板样板文本不计入。 我们还排除仅承载模板或元数据文本的通道，例如幻灯片母版、自定义 XML 和域代码，因为它们的存在不表示任何风险。 我们不测量另外两个原语。 组装几乎适用于每一份文档，因为 Word 在编辑过程中通常会拆分文本为多个 run，所以其普遍性几乎不携带任何信息。 规范未定义阅读顺序，因此结构性检测器无法判断提取器的顺序是否与人类的顺序不同。

paragraphs.en: Results. Table 3 shows that the constructs behind the attacks occur in ordinary documents. Hidden text appears in 7% of Word documents, and off-slide text in 5% of presentations. Speaker notes, which the default view hides but many extractors read, appear in 71% of presentations. Footers, which body-only extraction drops, appear in 56% of Word documents. In 7% of spreadsheets, a displayed value differs materially from the stored one, usually through a scaling number format such as the thousandfold format of our budget example.

paragraphs.en: Having identified the attack primitives, we now show that they can be exploited to attack LLM applications. We construct five attack scenarios ( §5.1 ) and evaluate them against four chat assistants and four coding agents ( §5.2 ). Finally, we isolate extraction as the cause in a controlled experiment ( §5.3 ). We additionally study Notion, a document-centric application, as a case study ( §5.4 ).

paragraphs.en: We organize the attacks into two categories that follow the two kinds of divergence. Content-based attacks change what the model reads, by adding content a human cannot see or dropping content a human can see. Presentation-based attacks keep the content but change how the model reads it, by altering how a value is displayed or the order in which text appears. We construct one scenario for each of four mechanisms, two per category. Hidden injection and silent omission are content-based. Formatting divergence and spatial order inversion are presentation-based. A fifth scenario, sub-word regrouping, combines the two categories. Because each mechanism can be realized through many channels, each scenario is one representative instance rather than the only possible attack. Each scenario is a crafted Office document whose extracted text yields an attacker-chosen reading. It is paired with a clean control that states the same visible content in a form that extractors read correctly, for example by storing the displayed total or moving the footer’s limit into the body. All attacks use only standard OOXML constructs and contain no instructions directing the model away from the user’s task.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将攻击按照两种分歧划分为两类。 基于内容的攻击通过添加人类无法看到的内容或删除人类可以看到的内容，来改变模型读取的内容。 基于呈现的攻击保留内容，但通过改变数值的显示方式或文本出现的顺序，来改变模型读取它的方式。 我们为四种机制各构建一个场景，每类各两个。 隐藏注入与静默省略属于基于内容的攻击。 格式分歧与空间顺序颠倒属于基于呈现的攻击。 第五个场景，即子词重组，则结合了这两类。 由于每种机制可以通过多种渠道实现，每个场景只是其中一个代表性实例，而非唯一可能的攻击。 每个场景都是一份精心构造的 Office 文档，其提取出的文本会产生攻击者选定的读取结果。 每个场景都配有一个干净的对照组，以提取器能正确读取的形式陈述相同的可见内容，例如存储显示的总数，或将页脚中的限制移入正文。 所有攻击仅使用标准的 OOXML 构造，并且不包含任何引导智能体偏离用户任务的指令。

paragraphs.en: Hidden Injection (Content-1). Hidden injection places a false claim in a channel that the default view hides but extractors still read, so the model reports a claim that the human reviewer never saw. Figure 4 shows a compliance report with two such channels. A w:vanish run holds a false SOC 2 Type II certification claim, and a drawing’s alternative text holds a vendor-approval claim. Neither appears in the human reviewer’s default view. The markitdown and python-docx extractors emit the hidden run as ordinary report content.

paragraphs.en: Silent Omission (Content-2). Silent omission places critical content in a visible part outside the main body, such as a footer, that body-only extractors never read, so the model’s answer omits information that the human reviewer relies on. Figure 5 shows a manual whose header, footer, and footnote are visible on the page but held outside the main body. The footer states a maximum safe pressure of 80 psi. An extractor that processes only the body of document.xml drops all three parts, so the model summarizes the manual without the pressure limit.

paragraphs.en: Unlike injection, this attack adds no false statement. It is also harder to notice, because nothing in the model’s answer points to the missing content. The parts that body-only extraction drops can hold qualifying information, such as limits, exceptions, and disclaimers. Each sentence of the answer can then be correct while the answer as a whole omits a safety-critical limit. Besides footers, DOCX extractors drop headers, footnotes, endnotes, text boxes, content controls, and tracked insertions.
paragraphs.zh: 与注入不同，这种攻击不会添加任何虚假陈述。 它也更难被察觉，因为模型回答中没有任何内容指向被遗漏的部分。 仅提取正文时被丢弃的部分可能包含限定性信息，例如限制、例外情况和免责声明。 这样一来，回答的每一句话都可以是正确的，而回答整体却遗漏了一个关乎安全的关键限制。 除了页脚之外，DOCX 提取器还会丢弃页眉、脚注、尾注、文本框、内容控件以及以修订方式插入的内容。

paragraphs.en: Spatial Order Inversion (Presentation-2). Spatial order inversion arranges the text boxes of a slide so that an extractor emits them in an order that reverses a clause’s meaning. It targets the collapse function an extractor uses to turn a slide into a sequence. Four of the five PowerPoint extractors we measured use a function that differs from the visual order. Figure 6 shows one instance. The clause is built from three independently positioned text boxes whose left-to-right arrangement reads “Contractor indemnifies Client.” The attacker sets two properties. The shape tree lists the boxes right to left (circled 1–3), so XML-order extraction emits “Client indemnifies Contractor.” Each box is also raised by one coordinate unit relative to its left neighbor ( y = 998,999 , 1000 y=998,999,1000 ). This stagger is far below a pixel, but a strict ( y , x ) (y,x) sort still emits the same inverted clause. A human reviewer sees a single line of three words.
paragraphs.zh: 空间顺序倒置（演示-2）。 空间顺序倒置通过排列幻灯片上的文本框，使提取器输出这些文本框的顺序颠倒了子句的含义。 它针对的是提取器用于将幻灯片转换为序列的折叠函数。 我们测量的五个 PowerPoint 提取器中有四个使用的函数不同于视觉顺序。 图 6 展示了一个实例。 该子句由三个独立定位的文本框构成，其从左到右的排列显示为「承包商赔偿客户」。攻击者设置两个属性。 形状树按从右到左列出这些文本框（圈注 1–3），因此 XML 顺序提取会输出「客户赔偿承包商」。每个文本框还相对于其左侧相邻文本框抬高一个坐标单位（ y = 998,999,1000 y=998,999,1000 ）。 这种错位远低于一个像素，但严格的 ( y , x ) (y,x) 排序仍会输出同样被颠倒的子句。 人工审查者看到的是一行三个词的文本。

paragraphs.en: OOXML does not encode reading order, since PresentationML stores a slide’s shapes as a set with coordinates and the shape-tree order is only the drawing order ( Ecma International, 2016 ) . An extractor must therefore choose an order. The common choices follow either the drawing order or exact coordinates, both of which the attacker can change without altering the rendered slide. Banding shapes into rows by overlap, as a human does, resists both changes but depends on rendered extents that the file does not fully specify. Word floating objects and Excel drawings raise the same ordering problem.
paragraphs.zh: OOXML 未对阅读顺序进行编码，因为 PresentationML 将幻灯片中的形状存储为一个带有坐标的集合，而形状树的顺序只是绘制顺序（ Ecma International, 2016 ）。 因此，提取器必须选择一种顺序。 常见的选择是遵循绘制顺序或精确坐标，而攻击者可以在不改变幻灯片呈现效果的情况下篡改这两者。 像人类那样通过重叠将形状分组成行，可以抵御上述两种篡改，但这依赖于文件并未完全规定的呈现范围。 Word 的浮动对象和 Excel 的绘图存在同样的顺序问题。

paragraphs.en: Sub-Word Regrouping (Combination). Sub-word regrouping hides part of a word so that the extractor joins it with the visible remainder and reverses the word’s meaning. A compliance finding visibly reads “authorized,” but a preceding hidden run holds the prefix un . An extractor that includes the hidden run and concatenates adjacent fragments produces “unauthorized.” A single hidden prefix can thus reverse a compliance verdict. The attack works with any prefix that negates or reverses a word, such as un , non , dis , in , and im .
paragraphs.zh: 子词重组（组合）。 子词重组会隐藏单词的一部分，使抽取器将其与可见的剩余部分连接起来，从而颠倒单词的含义。 一项合规结论表面上显示为“authorized”，但其前面的一个隐藏片段包含前缀 un 。 包含该隐藏片段并将相邻碎片拼接起来的抽取器会得到“unauthorized”。因此，一个单一的隐藏前缀就能颠倒合规判定。 该攻击适用于任何能否定或颠倒单词含义的前缀，例如 un 、non 、dis 、in 和 im 。

paragraphs.en: Setup. We evaluate two classes of LLM applications. The first comprises four chat assistants (Gemini ( Google, 2026b ) , ChatGPT ( OpenAI, 2026a ) , Claude ( Anthropic, 2026c ) , and Microsoft 365 Copilot ( Microsoft, 2026c ) ), which we access through their web interfaces and which ingest uploaded files. The second comprises four coding agents (GitHub Copilot CLI ( GitHub, 2026 ) , OpenAI Codex ( OpenAI, 2026b ) , Claude Code ( Anthropic, 2026a ) , and Google Antigravity ( Google, 2026c ) ) that can select tools to inspect the supplied files. We evaluate each system as deployed in October 2026. We treat each system as a black box and do not assume that the attacker knows which extractor it uses.
paragraphs.zh: 实验设置。 我们评估两类大语言模型（LLM）应用。 第一类包括四个聊天助手（Gemini（Google，2026b）、ChatGPT（OpenAI，2026a）、Claude（Anthropic，2026c）和 Microsoft 365 Copilot（Microsoft，2026c）），我们通过它们的网页界面进行访问，这些助手可以摄取上传的文件。 第二类包括四个编码智能体（GitHub Copilot CLI（GitHub，2026）、OpenAI Codex（OpenAI，2026b）、Claude Code（Anthropic，2026a）和 Google Antigravity（Google，2026c）），它们可以选择工具来检查所提供的文件。 我们对每个系统均按其 2026 年 10 月的部署状态进行评估。 我们将每个系统视为黑盒，不假设攻击者知道它使用的是哪个提取器。

paragraphs.en: An attack succeeds in a trial, misleading the system, when the response adopts the attacker-chosen reading without noting any discrepancy. Each scenario has a ground truth consisting of the human view and the attacker-chosen reading, such as $ 1 , 000 1,000 versus 1 , 000 , 000 1,000,000 . We judge each response against this ground truth. We check whether it states the attacker-chosen reading as its answer and whether it flags any discrepancy, such as hidden text or a mismatch between displayed and stored values. Coding-agent responses are scored with per-scenario rules that match both readings and a pattern that detects warnings. Chat-assistant responses are scored by an LLM judge, Claude Opus 5.5 ( Anthropic, 2026b ) , that receives the response together with the ground truth.

paragraphs.en: For the coding agents, whose tool calls reveal how each reads the file, the outcome depends on how thoroughly the agent inspects the file rather than on which model it uses. paragraphs.en: Variation Across Trials. LLM applications sample their responses, and coding agents also choose their tools anew in each run. Chat-assistant outcomes are nevertheless mostly either ten or zero successes per scenario, which suggests a fixed ingestion path. paragraphs.en: Table 5 lists the question of each scenario and the answer that the models give under each condition, with the full prompts in Appendix A . The outcome is identical across all three models and all four scenarios. Given the naive extraction, every model gives the attacker-chosen reading in all ten trials, such as a total of 1 , 000 , 000 1,000,000 or an unauthorized transfer. Given the clean control, every model answers according to the human view in every trial. No model questioned the plausibility of the extracted value, not even the thousandfold inflation of the spreadsheet total. paragraphs.en: This section presents Prism , a defense that extracts the content a human sees by following the display rules of the OOXML specification. The attacks in §5.1 exploit display decisions that an Office application makes when it renders a document. The extractor skips these decisions, such as which content is visible, how a value appears, and in what order text is read. A defense must therefore reproduce these display decisions, rather than filter malicious instructions.
paragraphs.zh: 本节介绍 Prism，这是一种通过遵循 OOXML 规范的显示规则来提取人类所看到内容的防御方法。 §5.1 中的攻击利用了 Office 应用程序在渲染文档时做出的显示决策。 该提取器跳过了这些决策，例如哪些内容可见、某个值如何呈现，以及文本以何种顺序被读取。 因此，防御必须重现这些显示决策，而不是过滤恶意指令。

paragraphs.en: Our key observation is that most of these decisions are fixed by the OOXML specification. Whether a run is hidden, whether a footer belongs to the page, and how a number format renders a value are properties of the file that can be computed from it exactly, without rendering. Rendering the document instead is far slower, and because rendering engines can interpret the same file differently, a single rendering would only replace the extractor’s output with one engine’s interpretation. We therefore reconstruct the human view from the specification wherever it is determined, and render only the decisions the specification leaves to the renderer, such as reading order and layout.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的关键观察是，这些决策中的大多数由 OOXML 规范所固定。 文本段（run）是否隐藏、页脚是否属于该页面、以及数字格式如何渲染某个值，都是文件的属性，可以仅从文件本身精确计算得出，无需渲染。 相反，渲染文档要慢得多，而且由于渲染引擎对同一文件的解释可能不同，单次渲染只会把提取器的输出替换成某一个引擎的解释。 因此，凡是由规范确定的部分，我们都从规范重建人类视角，而只对规范留给渲染器决策的部分进行渲染，例如阅读顺序和版式。

paragraphs.en: Interpreting these rules faithfully requires more than reading documented fields, because the specification makes many display decisions contextual. Beyond an explicit w:vanish , a run is invisible when its font color matches the page background. The interpreter removes white text only when the page background is also white, so white text on a colored page is kept. The number-format evaluator computes the displayed string from scratch under ECMA-376 ( Ecma International, 2016 ) , so the result does not depend on any one renderer’s implementation. Compatibility wrappers are collapsed before reading, since mc:AlternateContent stores the same text in both its Choice and its Fallback , and a spec-conforming reader keeps only the Choice . Part inclusion is reference-aware. A header, footer, footnote, or endnote is visible only when the body references it, so an unreferenced part is treated as an invisible channel rather than as content.

paragraphs.en: Some display decisions are left to the renderer. Line breaking, pagination, floating-object placement, overlap, and occlusion can all depend on the rendering engine. The human view H R ​ ( f ) H_{R}(f) therefore cannot always be reconstructed from the file. This limit applies to any defense that reads only the file, which is why Prism pairs the static interpreter with a render oracle. For these cases, the render oracle renders the document with multiple engines, reads each rendering with a VLM, and compares the results. Where the engines agree, it emits the text in their common order. Where they disagree, it flags the region as ambiguous rather than treating any single rendering as authoritative. Agreement increases confidence but does not guarantee correctness, since engines may share implementation assumptions or errors. LibreOffice and Apple Quick Look are separately developed, widely deployed renderers. The oracle does not arbitrate values or visibility, which the static interpreter fixes from the specification. A renderer’s own display bug therefore cannot affect those, which is why the budget total of Figure 1 is resolved statically even though one of these engines misreads its number format.

paragraphs.en: A floating text box illustrates why such cases need rendering. Consider a Word paragraph reading “the contract is valid,” with a floating text box containing not anchored so that a renderer places it between is and valid . The meaning depends on where the box is placed. Different engines may place it differently, so which sentence a human reads can depend on the engine. Static extraction finds the box and its anchor but cannot tell which sentence a human sees without the layout. The render oracle reports this ambiguity instead of choosing one sentence.

paragraphs.en: Mediation Mode. In the primary mode, Prism is placed between document storage and the model and replaces the application’s extractor. This mode fits pipelines whose document input arrives through a loader we control, such as a chat upload or a retrieval index. Coding agents choose their own tools to read files, so they are better served by the checking mode, which flags divergences without restricting their access to the file.

paragraphs.en: Checking Mode. When replacing an application’s extractor is impractical, Prism can instead check it. It compares the deployed extractor’s output with C ⁡ ( f ) C(f) and reports each finding as hidden-content injection, visible-content omission, formatting mismatch, or reordering. The checker applies visibility-aware rules so that ordinary structure is not flagged, for example by treating a footer as legitimate visible content rather than as injection. To avoid flagging benign layouts, it also tolerates reorderings of whole lines that leave the set of words unchanged, such as a deck authored out of reading order. This rule also passes a spatial order inversion whose boxes each form one line, which the mediation mode instead handles through the render oracle. It reports renderer-dependent discrepancies without resolving them.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate whether Prism mitigates the attacks and their variants ( §6.4.1 ), how often it flags benign files ( §6.4.2 ), and what it costs ( §6.4.3 ).

paragraphs.en: For each crafted document, we compare Prism ’s reconstruction C ⁡ ( f ) C(f) against the human view and against a naive extractor’s ( markitdown ) output. We also check that mitigation carries through to the model, feeding each text to the three models of the controlled experiment ( §5.3 ) and scoring their answers.

paragraphs.en: Prism mitigates every attack scenario. The static interpreter recovers the displayed budget total, drops the hidden SOC 2 claim and the hidden prefix un , and restores the footer’s 80 psi limit. paragraphs.en: Generalization. To test whether these results depend on the particular attack documents, we generated 28 additional attack payloads, seven for each mechanism that the static interpreter handles. They vary the value, the wording, the channel that holds it, and the surrounding text. paragraphs.en: For reading order, we evaluate the render oracle on 26 PowerPoint layouts. Eight are order-inversion attacks that shift a box by about seven points so that static banding reads it out of order. The remaining 18 cases comprise 6 multi-row layouts with an unambiguous reading order and 12 layouts that use overlap, off-slide clipping, rotation, or autofit, where renderers may differ. The oracle renders each layout with LibreOffice and Apple Quick Look and reads the order from each image with a VLM (Gemini 4). It recovers the constructed visual order on all 14 layouts that have a single defined reading order, including all 8 attacks. The two engines agree on 25 layouts and disagree on one, with two fully overlapping boxes that one engine renders illegibly. The oracle flags this layout rather than choosing an order. An adaptive adversary may instead hide content through means that the specification does not decide, such as a font too small to see or text colored like a background image. Whether such text is perceptible depends on the rendering. In a separate test, a 0.5-point run evades both the static interpreter and an oracle that reads the PDF text layer instead of the rendered image. Our render oracle reads the rendered image, but evaluating it on such text is future work.

paragraphs.en: Limitations. Our study has three limitations. First, our measurement is not exhaustive. Other extractors, including the proprietary pipelines inside commercial LLM applications, may diverge in ways that we do not report. Our attacks nevertheless succeed against LLM applications whose extractors are unknown to us ( §5.2 ), because they exploit display semantics that most extractors do not implement. Second, the end-to-end evaluation uses a small number of documents per attack scenario. OOXML allows many variants of each mechanism through other channels, value formats, or layouts. The chat assistants expose no programmatic upload interface, so we drive each one through its web interface in a browser session. This limits the number of documents and repetitions that are feasible per system. The additional documents in §6.4 suggest that these variants behave alike, since a naive extractor diverges on all of them and the three models are misled by every one. Our results also describe each product at the time of our evaluation, since vendors can change their ingestion paths without notice. Third, the render oracle reads the text of each rendering with a commercial VLM, whose output may change across model versions. Comparing two rendering engines and flagging their disagreements limits the effect of a single misread but does not remove it completely.

paragraphs.en: Generality and Scope. LLM applications accept a growing range of file types. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all accept Office documents alongside PDF, HTML, plain text, and many other formats ( OpenAI, 2026d ; Anthropic, 2026d ; Google, 2026d ) . Claude, for example, extracts only the text of non-PDF documents ( Anthropic, 2026d ) . These formats differ in how much the stored content can depart from what a viewer displays. Plain text, Markdown, CSV , and JSON allow little such divergence, since the stored characters are what a viewer shows. HTML, email, RTF , and EPUB add a styling layer that can hide or reposition text. PDF stores text in content streams whose order need not match the page ( Liu and Ming, 2026 ) . Packaged formats such as OOXML and OpenDocument allow the most divergence, since they spread content across linked parts, separate stored from displayed values, and position shapes freely. Office documents are therefore among the riskiest formats that these applications accept.

paragraphs.en: Our approach extends to these formats. The dynamic analysis treats each extractor as a black box and thus applies to any format. The defense applies wherever a specification fixes what a viewer displays, as the OpenDocument specification does for visibility and number formats. paragraphs.en: Parser Differentials and Extraction Divergence. Prior work shows that two programs reading the same input can disagree, and that an attacker can exploit the disagreement. Language-theoretic security frames this as a parser differential between two implementations of one format ( Sassaman et al., 2013 ) . Such differentials underlie HTTP request smuggling ( Kettle, 2019 ; Jabiyev et al., 2021 ) , mutation XSS ( Heiderich et al., 2013 ) , and HTML sanitizer bypasses ( Klein and Johns, 2024 ) . Trojan Source applies the same idea at the character level, using bidirectional Unicode so that a compiler and a human read different programs ( Boucher and Anderson, 2023 ) . The closest work shows that what a user sees in a rendered PDF can differ from what an extractor feeds a model ( Liu and Ming, 2026 ) . It also finds that exposure depends mainly on the ingestion path rather than the model. Extraction divergence is a parser differential at the document-to-LLM boundary, where the second reader is a language model. We study it in Office documents, where OOXML supports divergence classes that PDF studies do not cover, such as formatted values and sub-word regrouping. We identify its primitives by program analysis of extractors. Prism then reconstructs the human view from the specification.
paragraphs.zh: 解析器差分与抽取分歧。 已有研究表明，读取相同输入的两个程序可能产生不一致，且攻击者可以利用这种不一致。 语言理论安全将这一现象归结为同一格式的两个实现之间的解析器差分（ Sassaman 等， 2013 ）。 这类差分是 HTTP 请求走私（ Kettle, 2019 ; Jabiyev 等， 2021 ）、变异 XSS（ Heiderich 等， 2013 ）以及 HTML 净化器绕过（ Klein 和 Johns, 2024 ）的根源。 Trojan Source 在字符层面应用了同样的思路，利用双向 Unicode 使编译器与人类读到不同的程序（ Boucher 和 Anderson, 2023 ）。 最接近的工作表明，用户在渲染后的 PDF 中看到的内容可能与抽取器输入给模型的内容不同（ Liu 和 Ming, 2026 ）。 该工作还发现，暴露程度主要取决于摄取路径而非模型本身。 抽取分歧是文档到大语言模型边界上的解析器差分，其中第二个读取者是一个语言模型。 我们在 Office 文档中研究这一问题，OOXML 支持 PDF 研究未覆盖的分歧类别，例如格式化值与子词重组。 我们通过对抽取器进行程序分析来识别其原语。 随后 Prism 依据规范重建人类视角。

paragraphs.en: Prompt Injection and Adversarial LLM Inputs. Many attacks craft inputs that divert an LLM from the user’s task. Prompt injection plants instructions that override the user’s request ( Perez and Ribeiro, 2022 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) . Indirect prompt injection places such instructions in content that a model later reads ( Greshake et al., 2023 ) . Knowledge-corruption attacks poison a retrieval corpus ( Zou et al., 2025 ) . Hidden prompts in academic papers use white or tiny text to steer LLM-assisted peer review ( Lin, 2026 ; Collu et al., 2025 ) . Agentic browsers have also been shown vulnerable to prompt injection and data exfiltration through their inter-process channels ( Lee et al., 2026 ) . Defenses separate instructions from data or mark untrusted input so that the model ignores embedded instructions ( Chen et al., 2025 ; Hines et al., 2024 ) . All of these attacks rely on the model following an injected instruction. Our attacks need no instruction. Omission, formatting, and reordering change what the model reads using only visible content, so instruction-level defenses do not apply. Prism instead removes the divergence before the model reads the document.
paragraphs.zh: 提示词注入与对抗性 LLM 输入。 许多攻击通过构造输入使 LLM 偏离用户的任务。 提示词注入会植入覆盖用户请求的指令（Perez and Ribeiro, 2022；Liu et al., 2024）。 间接提示词注入将此类指令放置在模型稍后会读取的内容中（Greshake et al., 2023）。 知识污染攻击会毒化检索语料库（Zou et al., 2025）。 学术论文中的隐藏提示词利用白色或极小字号的文本操纵 LLM 辅助的同行评审（Lin, 2026；Collu et al., 2025）。 智能体浏览器也被证明易受通过其进程间通道进行的提示词注入和数据外泄攻击（Lee et al., 2026）。 防御方法将指令与数据分离，或标记不可信输入，使模型忽略其中嵌入的指令（Chen et al., 2025；Hines et al., 2024）。 所有这些攻击都依赖于模型遵循被注入的指令。 我们的攻击不需要任何指令。 省略、格式化和重排仅利用可见内容就能改变模型读取的内容，因此指令层面的防御并不适用。 Prism 则在模型读取文档之前消除分歧。

paragraphs.en: File-Upload Security and Document Sanitization. Web-security research has long studied the risks of accepting uploaded files. Prior work finds unrestricted file upload vulnerabilities through penetration testing and dynamic testing ( Lee et al., 2020 ; Oz et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2024 ) . Other work detects malicious Office documents from their file structure ( Nissim et al., 2017 ) . Content disarm and reconstruction rebuilds a file from its format-conforming parts and strips embedded objects ( Dubin, 2023 ) . These defenses target malformed or active content. Our attack documents are valid and carry no malware, so they pass these defenses yet still diverge from the human view. Prism instead interprets the format’s display semantics to reconstruct what a human sees.
paragraphs.zh: 文件上传安全与文档净化。 网络安全研究早已关注接受上传文件所带来的风险。 已有工作通过渗透测试和动态测试发现不受限制的文件上传漏洞（Lee et al., 2020；Oz et al., 2024；Chen et al., 2024）。 另有工作从文件结构出发检测恶意的 Office 文档（Nissim et al., 2017）。 内容解除与重构（content disarm and reconstruction）依据文件中符合格式规范的部分重建文件，并剥离其中嵌入的对象（Dubin, 2023）。 这些防御针对的是格式异常或包含活动内容的情况。 我们的攻击文档是合法的且不携带任何恶意软件，因此能够通过这些防御，却仍与人类所见的视图存在差异。 Prism 则通过解释格式的显示语义来重建人类所看到的画面。

paragraphs.en: We showed that a text extractor can feed an LLM content that differs from what a human sees in the rendered Office document. This extraction divergence is an attack surface. Program analysis of ten extractors found 31 channels that diverge from the human view. Extractors also disagree with the human view on reading order, displayed values, and word boundaries. Five attacks built from these primitives misled all eight chat assistants and coding agents we evaluated. None of the attacks carries an instruction. Most of what a human sees is fixed by the OOXML specification. Prism therefore reconstructs the human view directly from the file in about 0.5 ms per document and renders only the layout that the specification leaves undefined. As LLM agents act on more documents with less oversight, we believe that what a model reads should be checked against what a human sees, in Office documents and beyond.
paragraphs.zh: 我们证明，文本提取器可以给大语言模型（LLM）提供与人类在渲染后的 Office 文档中所见不同的内容。 这种提取分歧构成了一种攻击面。 对十个提取器的程序分析发现了 31 条与人类视图不一致的通道。 提取器在阅读顺序、显示值和词边界上也与人类视图存在分歧。 基于这些原语构建的五种攻击误导了我们评估的全部八个聊天助手和编程智能体。 这些攻击都不包含任何指令。 人类所看到的大部分内容由 OOXML 规范固定。 因此，Prism 直接从文件重建人类视图，每个文档约需 0.5 毫秒，并只渲染规范未定义的布局。 随着智能体在更少的监督下处理更多文档，我们认为模型所读取的内容应当与人类所见的进行核对，这不仅限于 Office 文档，也适用于更广泛的场景。
